statement: A committed test for a guard proves each check only if disabling that check, and each entry of a refusal list, makes the test fail with that check named; a bare toThrow() lets a later check stand in. 2026-11-09, cejel #694 (issue 689), my own near miss twice. First, the 176-case mutation test still passed with the inputs:/outputs: key check removed; disabling each check in turn found it, and two quoted duplicate-key cases outside the hashed region were added. Then Pass A showed that removing NEL, LS, PS, the lone CR, U+3000 or the C0 range from the invisible-character regex, or any of the four pre-checks, still left every case throwing, because the canonical runs: comparison refused the same manifests. Fix (#694): each refused case asserts its refusal message, the free region above inputs: gets its own line-break, marker and per-character cases, and each of 28 single-entry mutants of the guard fails at least 2 of 240 tests.
